title: Rav Hamnuna (II), Rav’s Student
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: In Bava Batra 110a it is explicit that he was Rav’s student, and in Eruvin 54a Rav said to Rav Hamnuna: “My son, if you have, do good for yourself,” etc. Likewise we find “Rav Hamnuna said that Rav said,” as in Eruvin 16b and 77b, Sukkah 21b, Kiddushin 65a and Avodah Zarah 19b; and in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:2, “Rabbi Idi, Rav Hamnuna and Rav Ada bar Acha in the name of Rav.” In Sanhedrin 17b they said: wherever Rav Huna says “they say in the school of Rav,” it is Rav Hamnuna. Hyman explains this as meaning that when Rav died in Sura and the academy passed to Shmuel, the academy of Sura was nevertheless not abolished, only they had no head of the academy. Rav Hamnuna was then the eldest in the group, and they made him head in the academy, that he should be the director, as we find in Jerusalem Talmud Maaserot, end of chapter 4, Sukkah 4:2 and Kiddushin 1:7: “Rav Hamnuna directs the group.” He was the director there until Rav Huna sat on Rav’s seat.

Hyman regards this Rav Hamnuna as greater than Rav Chisda, as in Berakhot 41b: Rav Chisda and Rav Hamnuna were sitting at a meal; dates and pomegranates were brought before them. Rav Hamnuna took and blessed over the dates first. Rav Chisda said to him: “Does the Master not hold this (which Rav Yosef — and some say Rabbi Yitzchak — said; in Dikdukei Soferim this is deleted, which Hyman endorses because Rav Yosef was their student)?” Rav Hamnuna said to him … Rav Chisda said to him: “Who will give us iron legs that we may listen to you” (that we may listen to you and always follow you — Rashi). Likewise in Shabbat 97a: “Rav Yosef said: This matter Rav Chisda was in doubt about, and Rav Hamnuna resolved it for him.” In Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 3:7 Rav Chisda raises an objection to Rav Hamnuna. Their disputes we find in Berakhot 22b and Shabbat 82a; “both of them say,” Shabbat 150a. Of his precious homilies, Hyman suggests that this Rav Hamnuna is the one who expounded in Berakhot 10a: “What is the meaning of what is written, ‘Who is like the wise man’? Who is like the Holy One, blessed be He, who knows how to make a compromise between Hezekiah and Isaiah … why do you involve yourself with the secrets of the Merciful One?” etc. Likewise there, 11b: “And Rav Hamnuna says: ‘Who chose us’ — this is the finest of the blessings”; and there, 31a, his precious homily in which he said: “How many great halakhot can be learned from these verses of Hannah.” Of those who speak in his name we find Rav Acha bar Ada, as in Eruvin 77b and Sukkah 21b, and Hyman proposes this reading in Avodah Zarah 19b and Kiddushin 65a. His death is mentioned in Moed Katan 25b: when Rav Hamnuna died, hailstones came down from heaven.

notes.text: Hyman’s temporary Sura academy leadership and relative age are interpretations, not a new appointment record. His deletion of the Yosef/Yitzchak attribution, oldest-in-group inference and identification of the homilist remain attributed. The full supplied Acha barAda form supports that connected abbreviation; always following and the hailstones report are retained.

The consulted Berakhot 41b retains Yosef, alternatively Yitzchak, in the dates/pomegranates discussion and continues with Hamnuna’s answer and the iron-legs remark. Hyman endorses a Dikdukei Soferim deletion; the exact edition remains uninspected here. His temporary Sura leadership, oldest-in-group and relative-rank conclusions are attributed, without globally binding a teacher formula or all Hamnuna homilies to one person.
